subtype: Family member in a medical emergency [Actor]
passage:
Dear Amandeep,
On Sunday morning Amma collapsed in the kitchen. My head filled with questions at once: which hospital, who has cash, should I ring Mama first? I made myself do one thing. I dialled 112 and gave our address slowly, twice. Then I unlocked the gate, switched on the porch light and asked Mrs Rao next door to sit with Amma while I waited by the road. Only after the ambulance had left did I call the relatives, and I sorted the papers and the money on the way to the hospital. She is being looked after. I will write again tomorrow. I am tired, but I am glad I did things in that order. Karthik

qa.q: What did Karthik do first when Amma collapsed?
qa.a: Karthik dialled 112 and gave the address slowly, twice.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling as the questions about hospital, cash and Mama crowded in?
qa.a: Karthik felt panicked and overwhelmed by the rush of decisions, but made an effort to do only one thing first.

qa.q: Why did Karthik leave the calls to relatives and the money questions until after the ambulance left?
qa.a: Getting help came first, and the other decisions could wait, so keeping that order stopped the panic from taking over.

qa.q: How might Mrs Rao have felt when asked to sit with Amma?
qa.a: Mrs Rao was probably worried but glad to help, since staying beside Amma gave a neighbour a clear and useful job.

grounding: Shows an adult whose parent collapses feeling panic and a rush of decisions, calling emergency services first and sorting the rest later.

subtype: Family member in a medical emergency [Actor]
passage: It was a Tuesday, in the lift lobby of our building. My father sat down on the bench and said he felt strange, and then he slumped sideways. Everything in my head started shouting: which hospital, do we have money in the account, who do I tell first? I shouted for the guard, dialled 112 and gave the block and floor. That was all I did for the first minutes, that and stay with him. Nikita, you asked what I would tell someone else. The calls to my uncle, the cash, the forms, all of that came after the ambulance. I still hear my own voice saying the address. Yamini

qa.q: Where did the narrator's father sit down and slump?
qa.a: He sat down on the bench in the lift lobby of the building.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when everything in the head started shouting?
qa.a: Yamini felt panic and a crush of worries, but chose to focus on calling for help and staying with the father.

qa.q: What was the right order of steps in Yamini's story?
qa.a: First shout for help, call 112 with the block and floor and stay with the father; the calls, the cash and the forms wait until after the ambulance.

qa.q: What might the guard have been thinking on being shouted for?
qa.a: The guard probably felt alarmed and hurried to help, since a resident needed urgent attention in the lobby.

grounding: Shows an adult whose parent collapses, with panic and many decisions, calling emergency services first and sorting the rest later.
